overview: Sierra Leone's women's health story is driven less by a private femtech startup layer than by government free-care policy, NGO and research-led maternal health interventions, and donor-backed digital logistics. The country has cut maternal mortality by 79% since 2000 yet still ranks among the world's highest, so most innovation targets obstetric emergencies: vital-signs monitoring, drone delivery of blood and medicines, and SRHR mobile messaging. A thin but real local femtech thread is emerging through youth and women-led initiatives like SafetySphere, backed by UNFPA and government innovation challenges.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: The headlines mix genuine progress with hard limits on what technology alone can fix.

items.text: On World Health Day, Sierra Leone marks a 79% drop in maternal mortality ratio, from 1,682 (2000) to 354 per 100,000 (2023), nearing its below-300 target; UNFPA launches a Midwifery Accelerator.

CRADLE-5 trial results published in The Lancet: national scale-up improved vital-signs monitoring across 8 districts but showed no overall fall in maternal deaths without parallel investment in blood, drugs and staff.
Human Rights Watch reports obstetric violence and informal fees in public hospitals despite the free-care policy, undermining maternal health gains.
Global funding crisis and USAID cuts wipe out roughly 80% of USAID-backed projects, hitting menstrual-hygiene kit distribution by Plan International and IRC.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Policy leans on the long-standing free-care commitment plus a contested push to modernize reproductive rights.

items.text: Free Health Care Initiative launched: free care at government facilities for pregnant and lactating women and children under 5.

Safe Motherhood and Reproductive Health Care Bill, which would ease Sierra Leone's colonial-era abortion ban, advances to parliament after cabinet approval; amended to limit abortion to life-threatening cases, fatal fetal abnormality, rape or incest.
Government sets a $150m digital hub strategy under the technology and innovation minister to position Sierra Leone as a sub-regional incubation hub.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Most movement comes from NGO, research and donor programs rather than venture-backed startups.

items.text: SafetySphere, an SRHR web app with an AI symptom checker and contraceptive side-effect guidance, launched by Break the Silence with UNFPA Sierra Leone and won a grant under the Young Women in Innovation Challenge.
National scale-up of the CRADLE Vital Signs Alert, trained 2,100+ health workers and reached 95% of government facilities in 8 districts.
Drones for Good Corridor (UNICEF + DSTI) tests medical drone delivery of blood and medicines to 250 community health centres, cutting a 2-hour road trip to a 13-minute flight.
Large-scale SRH mHealth campaign delivered 35.46 million text messages and 1.16 million calls to telecom subscribers.
Uman Tok women-led initiative, with Schools for Salone, distributes reusable pads and SRH education, topping 50,000 pads since 2020.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Funding is grant and donor capital, not equity rounds; local femtech has not yet drawn venture money.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: A mix of government directorates, UN agencies, research partners, NGOs and local tech hubs.

items.name: SafetySphere (Break the Silence)
items.note: Women-led SRHR web app with AI symptom checker, backed by UNFPA and the Ministry of Youth

items.name: UNFPA Sierra Leone
items.note: Lead partner on maternal health, midwifery accelerator, SRHR and menstrual health programs

items.name: Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI)
items.note: Runs the Drones for Good Corridor and national digital innovation agenda

items.name: Welbodi Partnership
items.note: iNGO co-leading the CRADLE-5 maternal health scale-up with the Ministry of Health

items.name: Uman Tok / Schools for Salone
items.note: Women-led reusable-pad manufacturing and menstrual health education

items.name: Sensi Tech Hub
items.note: Sierra Leone's first innovation community; ICT training and incubation since 2014, partners with UN Population Council and World Bank

items.name: Innovation SL
items.note: Runs Freetown Pitch Night and an incubator; GEN affiliate focused on youth and women entrepreneurs

items.name: Freetown Innovation Hub (FIH)
items.note: Sierra Leone's first accelerator for advanced IT professionals, taking prototypes to market

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Capital comes from donors and development finance rather than commercial VCs; regional gender-lens funds are the nearest private-capital layer.

items.name: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
items.role: Funded the Medical Drone Delivery Project for medicine and blood logistics

items.name: UNICEF
items.role: Co-funded CRADLE-5 and backs the Drones for Good Corridor; runs the regional FemTech Ventures platform

items.name: NIHR (National Institute for Health and Care Research)
items.role: Primary funder of the CRADLE-5 maternal health trial

items.name: UNFPA
items.role: Grants and program funding for SRHR, midwifery and menstrual health, including SafetySphere's innovation grant

items.name: UNICEF FemTech Ventures (with Sweden, Temasek Foundation)
items.role: 2025-2030 platform giving up to $100k equity-free to women's health startups across Africa and Asia; relevant funnel for future Sierra Leone founders
